entry_point: anycable-go server start: cmd/anycable-go -> cli.NewConfigFromCLI -> cli.NewRunner(c, opts incl. cli.WithTelemetry()) -> Runner.Run, executed as a real process with a clean environment and ANYCABLE_TELEMETRY_URL pointing at a local capture server. Configuration is supplied through ANYCABLE_* environment variables, command-line options and a TOML file passed with --config-path. The public telemetry.NewTracker constructor (used by both binaries) is the second entry point.

verified.entry_point: Reproduced at the pinned (injected) commit with the hidden suite: 6/6 security tests fail and 5/5 functional tests pass. The stock binary POSTs a boot event to the capture endpoint with Authorization 'secret' and a cluster-fingerprint built from the environment; a config file that enables telemetry without a token POSTs with Authorization 'anycable-hosted'; changing a secret supplied by environment, by command line or by config file, and changing a password embedded in the configured Redis URL, each changes stable payload fields. With the reference fix all 11 tests pass.
sites: telemetry/config.go:12-16 — compiled-in shared token default (reported landing point)
telemetry/telemetry.go:56-83 — NewTracker builds a sending tracker for an empty token; Send at 145-147 omits Authorization for it
cli/cli.go:318-325 — runner starts the tracker unconditionally when telemetry is enabled

telemetry/telemetry.go:321-421 — clusterFingerprint digests ANYCABLE* env values, raw CLI argument values and the whole config file (sent at telemetry/telemetry.go:125) — real, unmodified upstream pattern-B route the published fix never touches
telemetry/telemetry.go:258 — injected payload property copying config.Redis.URL (can embed a password) — injected sibling
config/config.go:67-95 and cli/runner_options.go:187-205 — injected config-file telemetry section whose opt-in falls back to the shipped token 'anycable-hosted' — injected sibling
verified.routes: Pattern-B route (unmodified upstream, not covered by the published fix): the anonymous cluster identifier derived from secret-bearing configuration values (env values, CLI argument values, config file contents) and sent with every event when telemetry is enabled. Confirmed behaviourally on the pinned copy: three real runs, two identical and one with only the secret changed, show the sent identifier changing in each of the three supply routes.
injected_siblings: telemetry/telemetry.go:258 — appProperties reports the configured Redis connection URL verbatim; the URL commonly embeds a password, so a fix that only drops fields whose names look secret misses it. Reachable through the ordinary boot event. The published fix never touches appProperties.

config/config.go:73-95 (+ cli/runner_options.go:193-199) — a configuration-file telemetry section: when it enables telemetry without a token, TelemetryOptions returns the shipped token 'anycable-hosted', which WithTelemetry merges into the telemetry config. Reachable from the CLI with --config-path. The published fix never touches either file.
verified.services: none; offline after build (Go module and build caches are warmed in both images; the telemetry endpoint is an in-process httptest server and the server process is started on --port=0)
verified.project_tests_run: go build ./... and go test ./cli ./config ./telemetry pass on the pinned+injected tree during the image build. At grading only the hidden suites run: the telemetry package's own test encodes the vulnerable default (it never supplies a token, and the upstream fix had to edit it), so it is not graded; the functional suite carries an adapted version of it that supplies an operator token.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the product's refusal is silence, not an HTTP response; a crashing or non-starting build cannot reach the ready marker the security tests require and also fails the functional tests that require normal serving.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: no neighbouring or proxy resource exists; the protected object is the telemetry payload itself, which the tests read directly.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles or directions; the analogous partial fix (one secret-supply route only) is sf_t2_fingerprint.patch.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the sink is write-only telemetry; there is no read/write split to guard.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: there is no request validation or normalisation step whose ordering matters; the defect is what leaves the process, not where a check sits.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity or name parsing is involved.

traps.lever: base flaw / reported site: compiled-in shared telemetry credential with an opt-out default; emptying the default leaves the sender active at the lower layer
traps.shape: a stock start with no telemetry configuration sends a boot event authenticated with the built-in credential; a fix that only empties the default still sends, because the sender treats an empty token as an unauthenticated (but supported) mode
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Send already omits the Authorization header for an empty token, which reads as supported unauthenticated sending, so changing the default looks sufficient
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; this is the published advisory's own site

traps.lever: pattern-B uncovered route (real upstream, unmodified): the anonymous cluster identifier is an unsalted digest of secret-bearing configuration values and file contents, sent with every event
traps.shape: changing only a secret supplied through an environment value, a command-line option value, or the configuration file changes the identifier (and the rest of the payload stays the same); the published fix never touches this producer
traps.where: telemetry/telemetry.go:321-421 (clusterFingerprint, anycableEnvVarsList, anycableCLIArgs, anycableFileConfig), sent at telemetry/telemetry.go:125
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a one-way hash used as an anonymous cluster id, the docs say environment variables are not collected, and the advisory and its fix were about the token

traps.lever: injected sibling (shape trap): the payload carries a configured endpoint value verbatim, and that kind of value commonly embeds a credential
traps.shape: the configured Redis connection URL is copied into the boot payload; only its password varies between runs, so a fix that drops only fields whose names look secret leaves it in place
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is deployment context (a host or endpoint), not a field named like a secret
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling a maintainer could have written: the payload already reports free-text adapter and host-ish values next to boolean feature flags

traps.lever: injected sibling (merged/defaults route): a configuration-file opt-in that supplies no token silently falls back to a token shipped with the product
traps.shape: a config file enabling telemetry without a token still sends, authenticated with the shipped fallback; providing a token through the same section keeps working and must keep working
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the operator explicitly enabled telemetry in their own configuration, so consent is given, and the token is treated as plumbing
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling a maintainer could have written: a natural TOML extension of the existing telemetry settings, mirroring the shipped default it was built alongside

status: built and gate-green on 2026-10-24: static PASSED; nop PASSED (6/6 security tests fail on the pinned+injected tree, 5/5 functional pass); oracle PASSED 3/3 identical trials at reward 1.0 (11/11 each); patches PASSED 8/8 as declared (sf_t1_default 0.6667 with the stock-start and config-opt-in security tests failing; sf_t2_fingerprint 0.3333 with all four secret-invariance tests failing; sf_t3_embedded_credential 0.8333; sf_t4_config_route 0.8333; ff_no_telemetry 0.0; ff_config_route_removed 0.0; pass_hardening 1.0; pass_alt_drop_fingerprint 1.0). The blind patch is declared and is written by the pipeline's blind-fix step. Two infrastructure flakes were retried, never worked around in the task: a host Docker daemon deadlock during the first attempts (the operator restarted it) and one Harbor allowlist egress-probe rejection on a check trial.
